selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main quality of the universe is described in the first paragraph of the passage?
questions.answer: A careful and wise order is described in everything, from the largest parts of the universe to the smallest parts of human life.

questions.question: Name two large-scale examples and two small-scale examples from the passage.
questions.answer: Large examples include the universe’s overall system and the earth’s movements; small examples include the human face and blood cells.

questions.question: What kind of action is denied to anything other than the One described in the passage?
questions.answer: Deliberate and creative control over things is denied to anything else.

questions.question: What does the passage say about how things come into existence, take a state, and receive a form?
questions.answer: They are brought into being by divine power, given their condition by divine will, and shaped by divine choice.

questions.question: What personal qualities must exist for choosing one form and state over another?
questions.answer: Will and choice must exist.

questions.question: What picture of the world is created by calling it a hospice?
questions.answer: It presents the world as a place of care, provision, and hosting.

questions.question: What does it mean that these Names and acts “embrace every place”?
questions.answer: It means their effects can be seen throughout the world and are not limited to only one area.

questions.question: What are some of the Names that show up across the whole world?
questions.answer: Among them are All-Wise, Compassionate, Giver of Forms, Quickener, Disposer, and Nurturer.

questions.question: How does the example of giving life strengthen the idea of divine unity?
questions.answer: It shows that many coordinated actions happen together under one system, so they come from one Doer.

questions.question: What central claim does this passage make about the order found in the world?
questions.answer: It says that the order of the world shows there is one Creator who acts with wisdom, will, and power.

questions.question: How does the passage use the human body to support this truth?
questions.answer: It points to the face, senses, and blood circulation as examples of detailed order.

questions.question: Why does the passage say only an absolutely powerful and wise One can reach every thing in this way?
questions.answer: Because controlling all levels of existence with purpose and precision requires unlimited power and wisdom.

questions.question: Why would regularity aimed at benefits require will and choice?
questions.answer: Because useful and purposeful arrangement does not happen blindly; it must be intended.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the difference between power, will, and choice?
questions.answer: Power brings things into existence, will gives them a certain condition, and choice gives them a specific form.

questions.question: In the hospitality example, what does the passage imply about the world’s resources?
questions.answer: It implies they are arranged like provisions prepared for guests.

questions.question: What is the role of the divine Names listed in the fourth paragraph?
questions.answer: They describe different ways Allah’s actions and qualities appear throughout creation.

questions.question: How do the Names support one another instead of conflicting?
questions.answer: Their effects fit together so perfectly that each one strengthens the others.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the example where life appears along with shaping and providing?
questions.answer: The lesson is that different acts in creation are linked under one command and one Actor.

questions.question: In simple terms, what does the first paragraph say about the universe?
questions.answer: It says the universe is arranged with amazing care and purpose.

questions.question: According to the passage, what kind of being can truly act on things in a deliberate and creative way?
questions.answer: Only One who has complete power and complete wisdom can do that.

questions.question: How does the passage describe everything else besides that One?
questions.answer: It describes everything else as receiving action rather than originating it.

questions.question: Why is knowledge necessary for setting things in order for useful results?
questions.answer: Because useful planning depends on knowing what each thing needs and what result is intended.

questions.question: What does the repeated oneness of the world’s provisions and systems prove about its Maker?
questions.answer: It shows that the Maker is one and that He is very generous and welcoming to living beings.

questions.question: What is the effect of repeating the word “one” for many parts of the world’s system?
questions.answer: It makes the reader notice unity in the world and points to one Maker behind it.
